title: How the Musketeers Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the history of the Three Musketeers: the Mars candy bar named after Alexandre Dumas's novel, the novel's plot and its basis in the real musketeer d'Artagnan, the Musketeers of the Guard founded under Louis XIII, and the evolution of firearms from the hand cannon through the arquebus, matchlock, musket, and flintlock, with the bayonet replacing the pikeman. They also discuss Dumas's life and prolific output, his mixed-race heritage, and his later reburial in the Pantheon. The episode closes with a listener mail correcting an earlier episode: Ralph McQuarrie, not George Lucas, conceived Darth Vader's helmet design.

entities.name: The Man in the Iron Mask

segments.title: Opening banter and Comic-Con
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about award-winning status and Comic-Con plans, then Josh proposes discussing the Musketeers. They shift to Mars candy and the Three Musketeers bar, which originally contained three flavors of nougat.

segments.title: The Three Musketeers novel and d'Artagnan
segments.summary: Josh summarizes Alexandre Dumas's novel: country youth d'Artagnan seeks to join the Musketeers of the Guard, meets Athos, Porthos and Aramis, and works into the fourth Musketeer spot amid duels and romance. They note Dumas wrote it about two centuries after the events, drawing on a semi-fictional memoir about the real d'Artagnan.

segments.title: Origins of gunpowder firearms: hand cannon
segments.summary: The hosts trace gunpowder's invention in China around 1000 and early hand cannons fired from a touch hole. Early guns were inaccurate and mostly psychological weapons. They digress into how warfare has progressed from fists to long-range weapons.

segments.title: Arquebus, matchlock, and the musket
segments.summary: The arquebus of the early 1500s added a shoulder stock for aiming. Matchlock ignition was unreliable in rain. The Spanish developed the heavier musket, called musquete or mosquete by the French and musket by the English, which needed a forked rest and a pikeman for protection.

segments.title: Flintlock, bayonet, and the term musketeer
segments.summary: The flintlock let muskets fire in wet weather and be smaller, and the bayonet replaced the pikeman. Anyone carrying a musket was called a musketeer. Louis XIII formed the Musketeers of the Guard as personal royal guards, who were expert swordsmen as well as musket users.

segments.title: Seventeenth-century France and the real Musketeers
segments.summary: The hosts describe French upheaval in the early 1600s, including the assassination of Henry IV, Louis XIII's accession at age nine, Cardinal Richelieu's power, and religious conflict with the Huguenots. The Musketeers were formed in 1622, grew to about 300 at most, and were disbanded in 1816 for lack of funding. The real d'Artagnan joined around 1632 and later commanded the Musketeers.

segments.title: Alexandre Dumas's life and reputation
segments.summary: Dumas was an extremely prolific writer who used assistants, and the novel was serialized in a magazine before publication as a book. Historians debated his status as a serious writer versus a hack. Hosts note his mixed-race heritage may have affected his reputation, and his remains were moved to the Pantheon in 2002.

segments.title: Listener mail: Darth Vader mask credit
segments.summary: A listener writes that Ralph McQuarrie, not George Lucas, conceived Darth Vader's helmet design, correcting an earlier Samurai episode. The hosts agree and note McQuarrie's contributions. Closing contact information is given.
